title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building an axiomatic 'analysis situs' (in the line of the 'tame topology' programme of the Esquisse). There is a set M (Ob F) of 'figures' in a 'contrée' carrying two structures. The first is a specialization/compatibility order <= together with a compatibility relation R, treated on p.68. The second, introduced on this page, is a relation written with a curly symbol (≼), meaning 'is a subdivision of'. The transcription renders this symbol as ≤, but p.70 explicitly distinguishes ≤ from ≼.

What the page says:
(1) Subdivision is 'of a very different nature' from the first order. In general there is no smallest (nor largest) element: two subdivisions F', F'' of the same figure F sometimes have a common lower bound (a common refinement) and sometimes do not.
(2) Definition. Two subdivisions F', F'' of F are called 'comparables' if they admit a common subdivision F''' with F''' ≼ F' and F''' ≼ F''. A small diagram sketches this. Grothendieck explicitly avoids the word 'compatibles', since it is already used for R.
(3) Definition. The contrée is called 'modérée' (tame) if any two subdivisions of the same F are always comparable. This is an abstract Hauptvermutung / common-refinement condition.
(4) He says he can state no interesting property of ≼ alone. The relevant properties concern the interplay of ≼ with disjointness and with ≤.
(5) Axiom C5. If F' ≼ F, then for every figure G: G is disjoint from F iff G is disjoint from F'.
(6) NB: this may be superfluous given C3. A margin note says it is superfluous after C6 and C10 together with the disjunction axioms.
(7) A margin remark says some property 'will be seen below to be true under the modération condition'.

On p.70 this becomes: F and F' have the same cospectrum / same support. As a corollary, cospectra are closed for both ≤ and ≼, so every F-support is a sub-contrée.

Modern reading: an abstract poset-with-refinement framework (like triangulations or cell decompositions ordered by subdivision). Here 'tame' means any two decompositions have a common refinement. This holds in PL and o-minimal settings and fails for arbitrary topological triangulations (Milnor 1961, the Hauptvermutung counterexamples). C5 says subdivision does not change the underlying point-set / support.
errors: No real mathematical error. Caveats: the terminology 'comparables' clashes with order-theoretic comparability, since F' and F'' need not satisfy F' ≼ F'' or F'' ≼ F'.

'Comparable' as defined need not be transitive in general. It is automatically an equivalence relation, in fact the total relation, only under 'modération'. The page does not discuss this; the margin hints that something becomes true only under modération.

ideas.what: Subdivision relation ≼ on figures as a second order, with no least or greatest elements and with common refinements not always existing
ideas.modern_name: refinement poset of triangulations / cell decompositions; cofiltered refinement
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 mentions tame topology and the need for an axiomatics, without this formalism

ideas.what: 'Modérée' contrée: any two subdivisions of the same figure have a common subdivision
ideas.modern_name: Hauptvermutung-type common refinement condition; o-minimal triangulation uniqueness up to refinement
ideas.usually_credited_to: Steinitz/Tietze (Hauptvermutung), Milnor (counterexample 1961), van den Dries / Shiota (o-minimal triangulation)

ideas.what: Axiom C5: subdivision preserves disjointness from any figure, i.e. F and F' have the same support / cospectrum

missed.claim: An abstract axiomatization of tame topology in which the Hauptvermutung (existence of common subdivisions) is isolated as a named axiom, 'modération', on an abstract 'contrée' of figures with a disjointness relation and two orders. The relation of this framework to o-minimal structures or to Shiota's / Hironaka's triangulation theory was never worked out.
missed.quote: On dit que la contrée est modérée si deux subdivisions d'une même F sont toujours comparables.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Grothendieck's tame-topology axiomatics from 1986 remain essentially unstudied. Comparing this lattice-theoretic approach with o-minimality and with the poset/frame-theoretic approaches to tame geometry could be of historical and possibly foundational interest.

deep.surprise_reason: A concrete unpublished piece of Grothendieck's 1986 tame-topology axiomatics: Hauptvermutung as the abstract 'modération' condition. The mathematical content itself is elementary, and the tame-topology programme is known from the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: The subdivision relation is written ≼ (curly), not ≤. Page 70 distinguishes ≤ from ≼.
'la catégorie[?] est modérée' should read 'la contrée est modérée' ('contrée' double-underlined; 'modérée' underlined).
'Il n'y a en vue[?] pas de plus petit' probably reads 'Il n'y a en général pas de plus petit'.
The diagram reads F' ≼ F, F''' ≼ F'' ≼ ..., i.e. a common subdivision F''' of F' and F''.
Margin next to C5: likely 'superflu après C6, C10, avec les axiomes de disjonction'. The NB likely reads 'Il semble superflu de le poser pour F, F' ... à cause de C3'.
